q: An organization is decommissioning self-encrypting SSDs that held confidential data. The drives will be resold to a third party. Which sanitization method is MOST appropriate?
c: Cryptographic erase followed by verification
A single overwrite pass of the full drive
Degaussing each drive before release
Quick-formatting the drive's file system

q: A newly created financial forecast must be classified before it can be distributed. Who is PRIMARILY responsible for assigning its classification level?
c: The data custodian
The security administrator
The data owner
The compliance officer

q: A company's retention schedule requires deleting customer records after seven years. Litigation is filed that involves records now due for deletion. What MUST the organization do?
c: Suspend deletion of the affected records under a legal hold
Proceed with deletion as the retention schedule requires
Anonymize the records so deletion can proceed safely
Delete the records but retain their cryptographic hashes

q: An organization selects a control baseline for a new system, removes the controls that do not apply to its environment, and adjusts the parameters of the rest to fit its risk profile. What is this process called?
c: Gap analysis
Scoping and tailoring
Control self-assessment
Certification and accreditation

q: Before assigning protection controls to its servers, laptops, and cloud instances, a security team wants confidence that nothing will be missed. Which activity MUST come first?
c: Deploying endpoint detection on all known devices
Encrypting data at rest across the estate
Conducting a penetration test of the network
Building and maintaining a complete asset inventory

q: A database administrator performs nightly backups, applies patches, and configures access permissions on a customer database according to rules set by the marketing director, who decides how the data may be used. Which role does the database administrator fulfill?
c: Data owner
Data steward
Data custodian
Data controller

q: An analytics team combines several internal datasets that are each classified at the lowest sensitivity level. The combined dataset reveals detailed customer travel patterns that would be damaging if disclosed. What is the BEST way to handle the combined dataset?
c: Classify the combined dataset at a higher level reflecting the impact of its disclosure
Retain the classification of the source datasets since no new data was collected
Raise the classification of every source dataset to match the combined sensitivity
Encrypt the combined dataset instead of assigning it a classification level

q: A newly appointed business unit leader must classify the datasets her unit produces, and her staff propose several possible criteria. Which criterion should PRIMARILY determine the classification level assigned to each dataset?
c: The cost of the storage systems where the data resides
The volume of records each dataset contains
The age of the data and how frequently it is accessed
The impact to the organization if the data were disclosed, altered, or lost

q: An organization uses seven classification levels. Audits show widespread mislabeling, and employees report they cannot explain the difference between adjacent levels. Two rounds of training produced little improvement. What should the security manager recommend FIRST?
c: Deploy an automated tool that applies labels based on content inspection
Simplify the scheme to a small number of clearly distinguishable levels
Introduce disciplinary consequences for repeated labeling errors
Conduct a third round of classification training with practical exercises

q: A security policy requires that all removable media containing sensitive information carry a visible classification label. What is the PRIMARY purpose of this labeling requirement?
c: To deter thieves by warning that the media contains protected information
To ensure anyone handling the media knows what protection it requires
To support periodic physical inventory counts of media assets
To demonstrate compliance with the policy during external audits

q: Weekly backup tapes containing regulated customer data are shipped to an offsite storage facility using a commercial courier. Which measure BEST protects the data during transport?
c: Select a courier whose insurance covers the replacement value of lost tapes
Compute cryptographic hashes of the backup sets before the tapes leave the site
Apply password protection to the backup catalog files written to each tape
Encrypt the tapes and track them with a documented chain of custody

q: A financial analyst exports selected fields from a database classified as Confidential into a spreadsheet for working analysis and stores it on a shared drive. Under standard handling requirements, how should the spreadsheet be treated?
c: As Confidential, because extracts inherit the classification of the source data
As a new asset the analyst may classify based on personal judgment of its content
As Internal, because only a subset of the original fields was copied
As unclassified working material until it is finalized and formally published

q: After a classification program rollout, employees can correctly state each document's label but continue to store, email, and dispose of sensitive documents in inconsistent ways. Which element of the program was MOST likely omitted?
c: A data classification policy approved by senior management
An awareness campaign explaining why classification matters
Handling standards defining required protections for each level
A formal process for owners to periodically review classifications

q: A rapidly growing company builds each new server manually, and vulnerability scans show that security configurations vary widely across systems. What is the BEST way to ensure new servers are provisioned securely?
c: Scan every server after deployment and remediate the findings individually
Deploy all new servers from an approved, hardened baseline image
Adopt the operating system vendor's default settings for consistency
Schedule an annual configuration audit across the server estate

q: Developers in a virtualized environment can create virtual machines on demand, and many run for months without appearing in the configuration management database. Which measure BEST addresses the resulting asset security risk?
c: Run scheduled network discovery scans to detect virtual machines already active
Restrict virtual machine creation to a small group of infrastructure administrators
Require provisioning through a workflow that registers each virtual machine at creation
Expand hypervisor capacity so development workloads can be centrally consolidated

q: An organization permits employees to access corporate email and documents from personal smartphones. Leadership wants corporate data removable when an employee departs, without touching the employee's personal content. Which approach BEST meets both goals?
c: Deploy a managed container that isolates corporate data and supports selective wiping
Require signed consent allowing a full remote wipe of any enrolled personal device
Prohibit personal devices and issue corporate-owned smartphones to all staff
Enforce a strong device passcode and full-device encryption through policy

q: A data governance review finds that new datasets receive classification labels only during an annual review cycle, leaving recently created data unlabeled and inconsistently protected for months. What is the BEST corrective action?
c: Protect all unlabeled data at the highest classification level by default
Increase the review cycle frequency from annually to quarterly
Assign labels when datasets are first shared outside the owning team
Require classification to be assigned when data is created or collected

q: A marketing team designs a sign-up form that requests date of birth, home address, income range, and employer 'in case the data becomes useful later.' Only an email address is needed to deliver the service. What should the privacy officer advise?
c: Collect the full dataset but encrypt the fields that are not currently used
Collect only the data required for the stated purpose of the service
Collect the full dataset after adding a broad consent statement to the form
Collect the full dataset but restrict access until a use case is approved

q: An analytics group wants to mine production customer records for trends, and legal requires the analytics copy to fall entirely outside the scope of privacy regulation. Engineering proposes replacing names and account numbers with keyed tokens, storing the key in a secured vault. Why is this proposal inadequate?
c: Tokenization breaks referential integrity, so trend analysis results become unreliable
The key vault becomes a single point of failure that must be assessed separately
The data remains re-identifiable while the key exists, so it is still regulated personal data
Keyed tokens can be reversed only by brute force, which regulators consider sufficient

q: An organization contracts a vendor to destroy decommissioned hard drives within 30 days of pickup. Which practice gives the organization the BEST assurance that the drives are actually destroyed?
c: Obtain serialized certificates of destruction and periodically witness or audit the process
Select a vendor that advertises compliance with recognized destruction standards
Include a liability clause making the vendor financially responsible for any breach
Verify the vendor's facility certifications during the initial procurement review

q: Before donating used laptops to a charity, an administrator plans to run a three-pass overwrite utility against each solid-state drive. Why does this plan fail to meet sanitization objectives?
c: Three passes are insufficient; flash media requires at least seven overwrite passes
Wear leveling remaps writes, so overwrites cannot reach all retired and spare flash cells
Repeated overwriting wears out flash cells, leaving the drives unusable for recipients
Overwrite utilities clear only the file system index, leaving the underlying data intact

q: A facilities team plans to sanitize a mixed collection of retired media — magnetic backup tapes, optical discs, and solid-state drives — by running everything through a degausser. What is the flaw in this plan?
c: Degaussing must be followed by an overwrite pass to count as a complete purge
Degaussing is only a clearing technique, too weak for media leaving the organization
Degaussing affects only magnetic storage, leaving optical and flash media readable
Degaussing destroys the media's future usability, which violates sanitization rules

q: An organization is drafting its first records retention schedule and must decide how long each record type will be kept. Which factor should PRIMARILY determine the retention periods?
c: The capacity and cost of the organization's archival storage platform
The classification level assigned to each record type
The retention periods adopted by peer organizations in the same industry
Legal, regulatory, and business requirements applicable to each record type

q: Arguing that storage is inexpensive, an operations director proposes eliminating data disposal entirely and retaining all corporate data indefinitely. From a risk management perspective, what is the MOST significant problem with this proposal?
c: Retained data enlarges breach impact and legal discovery exposure without adding value
Storage costs will eventually exceed the operations budget as data accumulates
Older data will fall below the deduplication ratios the storage platform expects
Backup and restore windows will lengthen until recovery objectives are missed

q: A vendor has announced end-of-support for the operating system running a revenue-critical manufacturing application. Replacing the application will take at least two years. What should the security manager recommend?
c: Decommission the system immediately to eliminate the unsupported platform
Isolate the system with compensating controls and document time-bound risk acceptance
Purchase extended support so the system can remain in place indefinitely
Continue normal operation, since the application itself is still vendor-supported

q: To satisfy a seven-year records retention mandate, an organization simply keeps every nightly backup indefinitely. When regulators later request specific records, staff spend weeks restoring and searching old backup sets. What is the BEST long-term remedy?
c: Rehearse restoration procedures so staff can retrieve records from backups faster
Reduce backup retention to exactly seven years so less media must be searched
Implement an indexed archive designed for retention and retrieval of records
Convert the nightly backups from incremental to full so restores are simpler

q: Investigations reveal that employees have been emailing spreadsheets containing customer account data to personal webmail accounts. Files are stored encrypted on the file servers, and all email connections use TLS. Which control BEST addresses this exposure?
c: Content-inspecting data loss prevention applied to outbound email traffic
Stronger encryption of the data at rest on the file servers
Enforcement of TLS for all connections to external mail systems
Multifactor authentication for access to the file servers

q: A healthcare firm processes highly sensitive records on a public cloud platform. Storage volumes are encrypted and all connections use TLS, yet the compliance team notes the cloud operator could still access record contents during processing. Which technology BEST closes this gap?
c: Bring-your-own-key management for the storage volume encryption
A dedicated virtual private network between the firm and the cloud provider
Transparent database encryption managed by the cloud platform
Confidential computing that keeps data encrypted in memory during use

q: A retailer wants to reduce the number of internal systems subject to its annual payment card compliance assessment. Card numbers currently flow through a dozen applications, though most only need a stable reference to each card rather than the number itself. What is the BEST approach?
c: Encrypt card numbers with a strong algorithm everywhere they are stored
Replace card numbers with vaulted tokens in systems that do not need the real value
Hash the card numbers so that stored values can never be reversed
Consolidate the applications onto one network segment protected by firewalls

q: A multinational insurer must comply with a law requiring that policyholder data for one country never leave that country's borders. The insurer is migrating to a global cloud provider whose platform replicates data across regions by default. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Encrypt the policyholder data so that any copies replicated abroad remain unreadable
Rely on the provider's standard terms of service, which promise regulatory compliance
Configure region-restricted storage and verify replication outside the country is prevented
Execute standard contractual clauses with the provider to legitimize cross-border transfers

q: A national retailer hires a cloud payroll provider that stores and processes employee salary data strictly according to the retailer's written instructions. Under most modern privacy regulations, which party is the data controller for this processing?
c: The payroll provider, because it physically stores and performs all processing of the data
Both organizations as joint controllers, because each one handles the data during payroll runs
The retailer, because it determines the purposes and means of the processing
The retailer's data protection officer, because that role is accountable for privacy compliance

q: A sales force travels constantly with laptops containing customer contracts and pricing data, and several devices have been lost or stolen in the past year. Which control BEST protects the confidentiality of the stored data if a laptop is stolen?
c: Full-disk encryption with pre-boot authentication on every laptop
A complex operating system login password enforced by policy
An always-on VPN connection back to the corporate network
Cable locks and tamper-evident asset tags issued to travelers

q: Laptops are routinely reassigned between employees within the same business unit, where all users are authorized for the same classification level. The drives never leave the organization's control. Per NIST guidance, which sanitization approach is MOST appropriate before reassignment?
c: Physically destroy each drive and install new storage in every reassigned laptop
Clear the drives with a verified overwrite before they are reissued
Purge the drives by degaussing them prior to handing them to the next user
Delete the previous user's profile and perform a quick format of the disk

q: An internal audit finds intact printed client files, including account statements, discarded in open recycling bins throughout the office. Which disposal practice BEST addresses the confidentiality risk for paper records?
c: Place strip-cut shredders beside every printer for employee use
Contract a recycling vendor under a nondisclosure agreement to remove documents intact
Label the bins as confidential and route them to the standard recycling stream
Collect paper in locked consoles and cross-cut shred or pulp it before it leaves control

q: During merger negotiations, a company must share due-diligence documents with outside advisers, prevent forwarding and printing, and revoke access to every copy, including files already downloaded, when the deal closes. Which solution BEST meets these requirements?
c: Enterprise information rights management that binds persistent usage policies to each document
TLS-encrypted email delivery of the documents to each authorized adviser
Password-protected archive files with the passphrase shared by phone
Visible watermarks embedding each recipient's name on every page

q: A CISO suspects that business units are moving regulated customer data into software-as-a-service applications that IT has never assessed. Which action gives the security team the BEST visibility and control over this activity?
c: Block every uncategorized cloud service at the perimeter firewall until it is assessed
Deploy a cloud access security broker to discover cloud usage and enforce data policies
Republish the acceptable use policy and require annual employee attestation
Review single sign-on logs to enumerate the applications employees access

q: A former customer invokes a privacy law's right of erasure and demands deletion of all records about them. National tax law requires the company to retain payment records for seven years. Which response BEST balances these obligations?
c: Erase every record about the customer immediately to avoid privacy law penalties
Deny the erasure request in full because statutory retention overrides privacy rights
Erase what the mandate does not cover, retain required records with restricted use, and document the legal basis
Ask the customer to consent to the company keeping all of the records for seven years

q: A classification program has stalled because twenty years of unstructured documents sit across file shares and collaboration sites, and no one knows where sensitive content resides. What is the MOST effective way to move the program forward?
c: Direct all employees to review and manually label their own historical files by quarter end
Encrypt every file share so that classifying individual documents becomes unnecessary
Set all legacy repositories to read-only until a business owner formally claims each one
Run automated discovery and classification scans, then prioritize labeling and controls by the findings

q: An analytics team stripped names and account numbers from a customer dataset, labeled it anonymized, and plans to send it to a university research group. Each record still holds full date of birth, gender, and postal code. What is the MOST important step before release?
c: Assess re-identification risk and generalize or suppress the remaining quasi-identifiers
Execute a data use agreement that bars the university from attempting re-identification
Encrypt the dataset with a strong algorithm for the transfer to the university
Assign each record a random study identifier and keep the linking key within the analytics team

q: When storage fills up, individual departments delete aging records at their own discretion. During litigation, opposing counsel alleges the company selectively destroyed unfavorable evidence. Which practice would BEST have protected the organization against this claim?
c: Retaining every record indefinitely so that nothing could ever be alleged missing
Suspending all deletion across the company permanently once any lawsuit seems possible
Destroying records only under an approved schedule, with documented disposition and a hold check first
Requiring employees to obtain manager approval by email before deleting any files

q: During an after-hours walkthrough, auditors find printouts marked Confidential left on desks in an office protected by badge-controlled entry doors. What should the information handling policy require?
c: Treat badge-controlled entry as sufficient protection for documents inside the office
Lock classified documents in approved storage containers whenever they are unattended
Shred every printed document at the end of each business day without exception
Prohibit printing of any classified information anywhere in the organization

q: A penetration test discovers an application server that was declared retired ten months ago still running on the network with stale customer data, absent from the asset inventory and every patch cycle. Which improvement BEST prevents a recurrence?
c: Increase the frequency of network vulnerability scans to find forgotten hosts sooner
Require certificates of sanitization for all storage drives that are sent for disposal
Relocate all servers that are awaiting retirement into an isolated network segment
Adopt a formal decommissioning procedure that updates inventory, removes access, and sanitizes data

q: A new analytics platform will process Public marketing content, Internal operational data, and Restricted financial results in one environment with a shared database and common administrator accounts. How should the security baseline for the platform be selected?
c: Apply the baseline required for the HIGHEST classification processed unless the data is genuinely segregated
Weight each dataset by its volume and select controls matching the average sensitivity
Apply Restricted-level controls only to the specific tables holding the financial results
Baseline the platform at Internal because that is the middle classification present

q: A regulation requires security event logs to be retained for twelve months. Keeping every log searchable in the SIEM's premium storage tier is consuming most of the security budget. Which approach BEST satisfies the mandate at sustainable cost?
c: Shorten log retention to ninety days to bring the storage spending under control
Continue retaining all logs indefinitely in the SIEM's fully searchable premium tier
Keep only aggregated statistics after thirty days and discard all of the raw events
Tier the storage: recent logs hot and searchable, older logs in compressed, integrity-protected archive until expiry

q: Marketing wants to send a customer list classified Confidential to an external analytics vendor. The classification policy defines internal handling requirements but is silent on external transfers. What MUST be in place before the data is shared?
c: A current SOC 2 Type II report from the vendor kept on file by the procurement team
A signed agreement obligating the vendor to handle, limit use of, and return or destroy the data per its classification
Strong encryption applied to the customer list before it is transmitted to the vendor
A cyber insurance policy that covers losses caused by third-party data breaches

q: Field technicians must carry equipment diagnostic files on removable drives to sites without connectivity. Several personal, unencrypted USB drives holding customer facility data have been lost this year. Which policy BEST balances the business need and the risk?
c: Prohibit the use of any removable storage device across the entire organization
Deliver targeted awareness training on safeguarding drives while traveling
Permit only organization-issued encrypted drives, enforced through endpoint device control
Rely on endpoint DLP content inspection to block sensitive files from being copied

q: Developers ask for a full copy of the production customer database to reproduce a defect in the test environment, which has fewer controls and broader access than production. What is the BEST way to satisfy the request?
c: Provide masked or synthetic data that preserves the structure and statistical behavior of production
Approve the copy after every developer signs an individual confidentiality agreement
Enable at-rest encryption on the test database before loading the production copy
Restrict access to the test environment so it is reachable only over the corporate VPN

q: A journalist extracts tracked changes, reviewer comments, and author details from a proposal document the company published on its website, exposing internal negotiating positions. Which handling requirement BEST prevents a recurrence?
c: Raise the classification level of all documents that are drafted for external audiences
Encrypt every document before it is transmitted to parties outside the organization
Require a metadata sanitization step that strips revisions, comments, and properties before any external release
Apply watermarks to final documents so the source of any future leak can be identified

q: An organization creates a role responsible for the customer dataset's quality, its business definitions, and the rules for its appropriate use, acting day to day on behalf of the accountable executive. Which data governance role does this describe?
c: Data custodian
Data steward
Data processor
Data user

q: A company is negotiating a five-year contract for a SaaS platform that will hold all employee HR records. From a data protection standpoint, which contract provision is MOST important for the end of the relationship?
c: Return of the data in a documented usable format plus certified deletion of all copies, including backups, within a defined period
Escrow of the provider's application source code with an independent third party
Provider-managed encryption of all stored data with encryption keys rotated on an annual schedule
A 99.9 percent availability commitment backed by meaningful service credits

q: Product design documents were classified Restricted during development. Three years after launch, much of their content appears in public patents and marketing material, yet all 40,000 documents still demand Restricted handling, slowing engineering work daily. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Keep the original classification permanently, since over-protection introduces no security risk
Allow each document's author to downgrade their own files whenever they judge it appropriate
Automatically reclassify the entire document set as Public on each product's launch date
Establish an owner-approved periodic reclassification review with defined downgrade criteria

q: A new privacy law grants individuals rights of access and erasure. A pilot request took six weeks to answer, and personal data was later found untouched in two systems no one had thought to check. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Procure a workflow portal that tracks subject request intake and response deadlines
Have legal counsel approve a standardized template for responding to individuals
Build and maintain an inventory of personal data mapped across systems, flows, and third parties
Script automated deletion routines in the CRM platform, the recognized system of record

q: Hospital applications exchange patient records through a third-party integration broker. TLS connections terminate at the broker, which can read every message. Compliance requires that the broker never view record content while continuing to route messages. Which approach BEST meets the requirement?
c: Negotiate stronger TLS cipher suites and shorter certificate lifetimes with the broker
Encrypt message payloads end-to-end at the application layer, leaving routing headers readable
Build IPsec tunnels between each hospital site and the broker's data center
Attach a cryptographic hash to each message that the destination verifies on receipt

q: The vendor of a storage array holding regulated data announces that support ends in eighteen months, after which no security patches will be produced. The array is otherwise performing well. What is the BEST management response?
c: Initiate a funded replacement plan now so the array is migrated before support ends
Wait for support to end, then react if scanners report exploitable vulnerabilities
Keep the array running indefinitely behind its existing storage network segmentation
Purchase spare hardware components now to extend the array's operational life

q: Remote employees regularly use hotel and coffee-shop Wi-Fi to reach an internal HR portal containing salary information. Which control MOST directly protects the confidentiality of this data while it crosses those networks?
c: Full-disk encryption deployed on all of the employee laptops
Multi-factor authentication required at the HR portal login
Endpoint detection and response agents on every remote device
An always-on VPN encrypting all traffic between the laptop and the corporate network
